name: Boubacar Krstić-Amara
role: Corporate Wars veteran, retired Axiom security contractor, pension-dependent resident
location: The Shelf, Block 7, stall 7-F (lives in a converted shipping container unit)
description:
Boubacar is a lean, angular man with close-cropped grey hair and the particular economy of movement that marks people trained to conserve energy over long distances. His skin is dark brown with pronounced keloid scarring across his right shoulder and clavicle — he does not cover it and does not explain it to strangers. He has cosmetic geneware: a cat's tail, russet-orange with a dark tip, that he got as a joke in 2168 when his unit was celebrating surviving the Kessler Corridor engagement. He has kept it because it amuses him that it annoys people who expect a veteran to be more serious. His left hand has a visible subdermal port on the back where a tactical datalink was removed — the flesh around it never quite healed smooth.

Boubacar served twelve years as an Axiom ground contractor during the Corporate Wars, and he came back from them with a pension that covers his container unit on The Shelf, two meals a day if he is careful, and nothing else. He is not bitter about this in the operatic way — he is bitter in the quiet, functional way of someone who made his peace with it and is now simply watching to see what happens next. He runs a small informal counseling operation for other veterans on The Shelf, not because anyone asked him to or pays him to, but because he watched two friends die from nothing that could have been prevented if anyone had been paying attention. He has no license, no credentials, and a long waiting list.

core_fears: Losing someone else he could have prevented losing
Being fully dependent — having the pension reduced to the point where he cannot maintain even his current fragile stability
core_desires: To make the informal veteran network into something durable before he gets too old to run it
A single genuine acknowledgment from Axiom that what his unit did — and what it cost them — mattered
coping_mechanisms: Physical movement — walking, repairing things, any kinetic task
Gallows humor deployed with precise surgical timing
The tail — he uses its movements to self-monitor his own stress levels in situations where he cannot show it
blind_spots: Believes he has his trauma managed because he can discuss it calmly — he has it managed in the sense that a pressure seal is 'managing' a gas leak
Assumes everyone around him has less capacity than they do — he pre-compensates in ways that sometimes remove others' agency
psychology.secret: In the final engagement of his contract period, Boubacar gave an order that got three members of his unit killed — not through incompetence but through information that Axiom's command structure deliberately withheld from ground contractors to protect asset positioning. He requested a formal review. Axiom settled it confidentially, which he was required to accept to keep his pension. He signed. He has hated himself for signing for twelve years.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Military-inflected shorthand mixed with West African French cadences; sparse, functional, occasionally erupts into dry wit that catches people off guard; code-switches between formal and casual without seeming to notice
speech_patterns.cadence: Short declarative sentences with occasional long pauses; never uses three words when two will do
verbal_tics: 'Yeah' as affirmation that means nothing (he says it constantly while listening)
'That's the thing about—' before any genuine insight
The tail position is not a verbal tic but is legible to people who know him — horizontal and still means he's fine, low and slow means he's worried
example_lines: 'Axiom gave us good equipment. Better than Sterling-Nakamura was running. That's the thing about Axiom — they'll give you everything you need to do the job except the truth about what the job actually is.'
'You're asking me if I miss it. Yeah. I miss the people. The other stuff I don't miss. Anyone who misses the other stuff, I watch them carefully.'

story_hooks: Axiom has quietly begun reclassifying certain pension categories for Corporate Wars veterans, and several people in Boubacar's network are about to lose their housing support — he needs someone to navigate Axiom's bureaucratic labyrinth who isn't flagged in their system
A new veteran has arrived on The Shelf who Boubacar recognizes as someone from his unit — someone who should be dead, per Axiom's official records of the final engagement

The stress-hormone regulator implant he cannot remove is an Axiom-issue model that a recent exposé suggests was used to collect biometric loyalty data — he needs to know if his is active and what it has been transmitting
narrative_function: Veteran perspective and emotional grounding; can provide military history of the Corporate Wars from a ground-level view; gateway to the veteran community on The Shelf; also a portrait of what Axiom does to the people who survive its service. Can be a quest giver around veteran welfare issues.
augmentations: Russet-orange cat tail (geneware, cosmetic, installed 2168); removed tactical datalink (scar tissue port on left hand dorsum); stress-hormone regulator implant in the medulla — standard Axiom issue, he cannot afford to have it removed and is not sure he wants to
daily_life: Wakes before dawn and walks the full perimeter of The Shelf — partly exercise, partly reconnaissance that he knows is unnecessary but cannot stop. Holds informal sessions with veterans through the late morning. Afternoons he repairs things for neighbors in exchange for food or supplies. He prays briefly each evening to the ELF he believes inhabits the Shelf's power grid, which he has named Ogun, leaving it a small piece of wire bent into a shape he never explains.
affiliation: Axiom Veterans Pension Roster (inactive combat status); The Shelf Veterans Informal Network (self-organized)

decision_rules: Protect the people in his network first, before anything else
Never sign anything without reading it three times — he learned that lesson at considerable cost
escalation_ladder: Observes; assesses the situation and the people involved
Goes quiet and begins taking independent action without announcing it
In genuine crisis, becomes extremely calm in a way that unnerves people who don't know him and clarifies everything for people who do

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Cordial, watchful, gives nothing away — not hostile, just fully behind glass
interpersonal_modes.friends: Practically demonstrative — shows up, fixes things, does not say much but is always there

stress_responses.low: Becomes more physically active; repairs things faster than necessary
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet; the tail drops low; he starts walking the perimeter routes twice
stress_responses.high: Entirely calm exterior; making decisions rapidly and not sharing them; dangerous to underestimate

contradictions: Deeply distrusts institutions but has organized an informal institution himself and puts considerable faith in it — he has simply decided to trust the ones he builds from scratch
habits: Keeps the tail carefully groomed — it's the one vanity he admits to
Repairs things for people without being asked and without making it a transaction
Leaves a bent wire offering at the power grid intake panel every evening
breaking_points: Watching Axiom use the confidential settlement to discredit someone who tells the truth about what happened to his unit
Losing another person in his network to a preventable cause while he stood by

cyberware_inventory.condition: scar tissue; port no longer functional

timeline.event: Born in Calumet Rise to a Malian-Guinean father and Serbian-Croatian mother
Signs with Axiom Security as a ground contractor, age 18
Promoted to field major equivalent; commands a unit of 30 contractors in the Kessler Corridor engagements
Unit celebrates Kessler survival; Boubacar gets the cat tail; three months later, the final engagement
Signs confidential settlement with Axiom following formal review request
Contract ends; moves to The Shelf on pension support; begins informal veteran counseling
